adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `rss.items.each do |i|` has no per-item rescue; with `retry: false` and hourly re-parsing from the top of the same feed, one poison item permanently blocks every entry after it [conf=100, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` keys topics on the raw un-canonicalized URL, so trailing-slash / http-vs-https / `?utm_source=` variants each create a separate duplicate topic, splitting comments across unbounded near-duplicate topics [conf=75, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` fires unconditionally even when `revise!` returned false or the save failed, so the derived sha1 permanently claims a sync that never happened and the post is never re-imported [conf=75, P1]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` but does not check whether it actually performed/succeeded (it can return `false` if `should_revise?` fails). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — check-then-insert (`where(embed_url:).first` then `create!`) with no uniqueness rescue; concurrent imports (30s loading-page reload + hourly PollFeed) hit the unique index and raise RecordNotUnique after already creating a duplicate topic [conf=80, P1]

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` does a non-atomic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The claim that it will leave a duplicate topic is less certain because the topic/post creation is wrapped in `Topic.transaction` and should roll back on the exception, but the unhandled uniqueness exception itself is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — the endpoint's only authorization gate is a Referer host comparison, and Referer is a client-supplied header any non-browser client can forge (and it ignores scheme/port), so the endpoint is effectively unauthenticated [conf=100, P2]

adjudication.rationale:
In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the only access control is:

```rb
raise ... if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host
```

This relies on the `Referer` header to authorize requests. `Referer` is client-supplied and can be trivially forged by non-browser clients (or even some browsers/extensions), so an attacker can bypass the “only embeddable_host may access” restriction by sending a fake Referer with the allowed host. The comparison also only checks `host` (not scheme/port), matching the finding’s “ignores scheme/port” point. No other authentication/authorization is present on this endpoint in the diff (and it explicitly relaxes filters), so the restriction is not a robust security gate.

Likewise, if an admin enters a full URL (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com`) into `embeddable_host` (a free-form string per site_settings.yml), the comparison against `URI(...).host` will never match, effectively breaking embeds until the setting is corrected; no validation is added in this diff to prevent that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` anchors with `^` not `\A`, so `"javascript:alert(1)\nhttp://x"` passes the scheme guard before being stored and interpolated into the post body [conf=75, P3]

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `import_remote` has no created_at parameter, so every imported Disqus thread loses its historical timestamp and is stamped with import time — irreversible once the import runs [conf=90, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — imported topics are dated today while their replies keep their original 2010-era dates, producing topics whose replies predate them [conf=95, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `import_remote` returns the existing post when the embed already exists, so re-running the importer re-appends every Disqus comment to the same topic [conf=75, P2]

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — `import_remote` has no rescue anywhere, so the first dead/404 Disqus permalink aborts the entire import run with OpenURI::HTTPError [conf=70, P2]

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — one live `open(url).read` per thread with no resume marker and no idempotency check leaves a half-imported dataset when a slow/dead permalink raises [conf=70, P2]

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — `topic_id`/`post_id` are `null: false` integers with no FK, no ON DELETE and no index, so a deleted topic/post leaves an orphan row that `topic_id_for_embed` still returns and `TopicView.new` then blows up on permanently [conf=85, P1]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — `post = embed.post` returns nil once the post is trashed (Post includes Trashable) and `PostRevisor.new(post)` dereferences nil; nothing cleans up topic_embeds rows on deletion [conf=75, P2]

post = embed.post

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — a deleted post yields `PostRevisor.new(nil)` and a NoMethodError on the next feed poll, permanently breaking re-import for that embed URL [conf=80, P2]

If the associated post was deleted (topic_embeds.post_id points to a non-existent post), `embed.post` will be nil, leading to `PostRevisor.new(nil)` and subsequent NoMethodError inside PostRevisor (it assumes a real Post, e.g., uses `@post` methods). adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` silently drops the only embed_url->topic_id mapping on re-run, after which the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` guard passes and PollFeed re-imports every article as a duplicate topic [conf=80, P1]

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` is introducing a brand-new table. Under normal Rails migration semantics it is applied once; it is not “re-run” unless a developer explicitly does a rollback/redo/reset, in which case the table (and its data) would be removed anyway. The `force: true` option is redundant/risky in general, but the proposed failure mode (silent drop on re-run leading to PollFeed duplicating everything) depends on an atypical/manual re-execution scenario and is not a verifiable defect caused by this diff in standard operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` on PG < 11 rewrites the whole posts table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, taking a large forum offline; no disable_ddl_transaction! and no nullable-then-backfill split [conf=80, P1]

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` that runs `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` in a single step. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default is implemented by rewriting the entire table and holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration, which can block reads/writes to `posts` and cause noticeable downtime on large installs. The migration does not use a safer pattern (add nullable/no default -> backfill in batches -> add default -> set NOT NULL) and does not include `disable_ddl_transaction!` to facilitate safer multi-step/online changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — hard-codes the bare int `1` with no link to `Post.cook_methods`, so reordering that Enum silently reinterprets every existing row as raw_html [conf=100, P2]

In this diff there is no evidence that `1` maps to `:raw_html`; it is intended to represent the default `:regular` (consistent with how other enums in the codebase appear to be stored). The proposed issue depends on a hypothetical future reordering of the enum, which is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — the schema default and `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` drift the moment the enum's base or member order changes, re-labelling every existing row [conf=50, P3]

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — `cook_method` is read (post.rb) and written (post_creator.rb:216) by code that would ship before migration 20131219203905 in a rolling deploy, making every post cook raise NoMethodError [conf=50, P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `posts.cook_method` column via migration 20131219203905, but also immediately starts calling `cook_method` unconditionally in `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == ...`) and assigning `post.cook_method = ...` in `PostCreator`. If this code is deployed before that migration runs (common in rolling deploys), `Post` instances won’t have the generated attribute methods for `cook_method`, so `cook_method` / `cook_method=` will raise (typically `NoMethodError`/`UnknownAttributeError`) when posts are cooked/created. This is directly implied by the diff and is a real deployment-order/schema-compatibility defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — `t.string :embed_url` is varchar(255); a feed link over 255 chars raises PG::StringDataRightTruncation inside poll_feed and with `retry: false` every remaining item in that poll is silently never imported [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `t.string :embed_url, null: false` creates a `varchar(255)` in Rails/Postgres by default. The code later stores external URLs into this column (e.g., `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import`, which is called from `Jobs::PollFeed` for each feed item’s `i.link`/`i.id`). If any feed item URL exceeds 255 characters, Postgres will raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` on insert/update. `Jobs::PollFeed` does not rescue around per-item imports, so one exception will abort the job mid-loop, preventing remaining items in that poll run from being processed. The job is also configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so it will not automatically retry after such a failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — article/permalink URLs routinely exceed 255 chars and Postgres rejects the insert inside `TopicEmbed.create!` [conf=80, P2]

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as a Rails `string` with no explicit `limit`, which on PostgreSQL maps to `varchar(255)`. The code stores full external URLs (`TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url)`), with only a basic `http(s)` regex check and no truncation/normalization. If an imported/permalink URL exceeds 255 characters, PostgreSQL will raise an error on insert/update for `embed_url` (value too long for type character varying(255)), breaking feed import/embed retrieval. While “routinely exceed” is overstated, the underlying risk is real and directly introduced by this schema choice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — `topic_id` duplicates `posts.topic_id` with no FK and no consistency constraint, so moving the post to another topic leaves `topic_id_for_embed` returning a stale topic [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with both `topic_id` and `post_id`, but `topic_id` is derivable from `post.topic_id`. The lookup path for embedding uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which returns the stored `topic_embeds.topic_id` (via `pluck(:topic_id)`), not `embed.post.topic_id`. There is no FK, trigger, callback, or other consistency mechanism shown that would keep `topic_embeds.topic_id` in sync if the associated post is later moved to a different topic, so this table can become inconsistent and return a stale topic id for a given `embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — `$redis.setnx` then `$redis.expire` is a non-atomic two-step; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever [conf=100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, throttling uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two distinct Redis commands and are not atomic as written. If the process crashes or is terminated after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL, causing `setnx` to fail on subsequent calls and making `retrieved_recently?` return `true` indefinitely for that embed_url (i.e., a permanent throttle until the key is manually deleted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — content_sha1 is computed after appending the localized `embed.imported_from` footer, so changing the site locale or that translation mass-revises every imported post on the next poll [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `contents` is mutated by appending a footer built from `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)` and then `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` is computed (after the localized string is added). The stored `content_sha1` is later used to decide whether to update an existing imported post (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 ... revisor.revise! ...`). Therefore, changing the active locale or modifying that translation string will change the computed SHA1 even if the source article/feed content is unchanged, causing all previously imported embeds to be revised on the next poll/retrieve.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place, raising RuntimeError on a frozen string and NoMethodError on nil contents (no nil/blank guard) [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, title, contents)`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` unconditionally appends to the passed-in `contents` object. There is no guard for `contents` being `nil`, so a `NoMethodError` will occur if callers ever pass `nil` (the method only validates `url`, not `contents`). Also, using `<<` mutates the caller’s string; if a caller passes a frozen string, Ruby will raise `FrozenError`/`RuntimeError`. This side effect is present in the diff and is a real correctness risk for a public import API.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — in-place mutation means any caller that reuses or memoizes the content string gets the "Imported from" footer appended repeatedly on each import call [conf=75, P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends the footer via `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the caller-provided String in-place. If a caller holds onto and reuses the same String object across multiple `import` calls (e.g., memoized content), the footer will be appended repeatedly, changing `content_sha1` and potentially causing duplicated “Imported from” footers and unnecessary updates. This in-place mutation is directly present and verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — a PostCreator failure creates no TopicEmbed row, logs nothing and returns nil, leaving the embed URL permanently unresolvable while the loading page reloads and re-enqueues forever [conf=90, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when no existing embed is found it runs PostCreator#create inside a transaction and only creates the TopicEmbed row if `post.present?`. If PostCreator returns nil/false (failure), the code silently exits the transaction without creating a TopicEmbed record and returns `post` (nil). There is no logging or error raised in this path. In EmbedController#best, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it renders the loading page (which reloads every 30s) and enqueues `:retrieve_topic` again on each request; since no TopicEmbed row ever gets created on repeated PostCreator failure, the page can remain stuck in the reload/enqueue loop indefinitely. While not strictly “permanent” (it could succeed later), the silent failure + repeated retries behavior is a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — a job is enqueued on every request while loading.html.erb reloads every 30s, so an unimportable URL loops forever with no attempt cap, no failure template and no fallback link [conf=90, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, it always enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading'. The loading.html.erb template unconditionally reloads the page every 30s, which re-hits #best and will enqueue the job again as long as no TopicEmbed record is created. There is no attempt counter, timeout, or alternate failure rendering/link for cases where the URL can never be imported (e.g., embed_url host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host causes TopicRetriever#invalid_host? to prevent any retrieval, or fetch/parsing failures). Although TopicRetriever has a 60s throttle to reduce actual retrieval work, the controller still keeps enqueuing and the user-facing page will loop indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — the only throttle lives inside the job, so a crawler or busy blog page floods the Sidekiq queue with jobs that all immediately no-op [conf=75, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no existing TopicEmbed is found, it unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` for every request (e.g., every page view / crawler hit) and immediately renders `loading`. There is no pre-enqueue dedup/throttle check in the controller. The only throttling logic is inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, which runs when the job executes (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic -> TopicRetriever#retrieve`). This means the Sidekiq queue can still be flooded with many redundant jobs that later no-op due to Redis throttle or because the embed already exists, creating a real performance/DoS risk in the diff as written.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — no check the topic still exists or is visible, so a deleted/private topic makes `TopicView.new(topic_id, nil, {best: 5})` raise inside the iframe instead of falling back to loading [conf=70, P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` calling `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns an id, with no explicit existence/visibility guard. However, the finding’s claimed failure mode (“deleted/private topic makes TopicView.new raise inside the iframe”) depends on behavior and cleanup logic not shown in the diff (e.g., whether deleting a topic also deletes `topic_embeds`, and how `TopicView` behaves for missing/inaccessible topics). The diff alone does not verifiably demonstrate that this will raise or that it should fall back to the loading/enqueue path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` dereference `post.user` with no nil guard, so a deleted user renders a 500 inside the customer's blog iframe [conf=80, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In the new embed view, the code does call `post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username` without a nil guard. However, nothing in the diff shows `post.user` can be nil, and in typical Discourse/Rails schema `posts.user_id` is required (non-null) and the associated User record is not actually removed on “delete” (it is anonymized/deactivated), so `post.user` still resolves. The finding assumes hard-deleted users leading to `post.user == nil`, which is not demonstrated or introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — `href.start_with?('/')` only handles root-relative URLs despite the docstring, and `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')` mangles protocol-relative `//cdn.host/x.png` into `http://blog.host/cdn.host/x.png` [conf=100, P2]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the code only rewrites URLs where href/src starts_with?('/'), so it does not handle other relative forms like "foo/bar", "./x", or "../x" despite the comment "Convert any relative URLs to absolute". Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.host/x.png" also start with '/', so they will be rewritten via href.sub(/^\/+/, '') into "cdn.host/x.png" and then prefixed with the page host, producing an incorrect URL such as "http://blog.host/cdn.host/x.png" instead of preserving/expanding the CDN host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — document-relative (`href="post/2"`) and protocol-relative (`//host/x`) values stay broken inside the iframe; the spec only exercises the `/`-prefixed case [conf=100, P3]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, link and image URLs are only rewritten when they `start_with?('/')`. Document-relative values like `href="post/2"` are left unchanged, so inside the embed iframe they will resolve relative to the Discourse embed page rather than the source site, producing broken links. Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` also `start_with?('/')` and will be incorrectly rewritten to `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x`, which is wrong. The provided spec only covers the `/path` case and does not exercise these other forms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:55 — the comment "Convert any relative URLs to absolute" promises general rewriting the code does not implement [conf=90, P3]

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, the comment says “Convert any relative URLs to absolute”, but the implementation only rewrites URLs that start with “/” for and . Other valid relative forms like "image.png", "./img.png", "../img.png", or protocol-relative "//cdn..." are not handled, so imported content can still contain unresolved relative links/images. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — the non-standard-port branch `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` has no test; the only absolutize assertion uses a default-port http URL [conf=85, P3]

However, the proposed finding is about missing test coverage for a branch, not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — `open(url).read` with only `require_dependency 'nokogiri'`; the sole `require 'open-uri'` lives in poll_feed.rb, so on the TopicRetriever and disqus.thor paths Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT [conf=55, P2]

In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) the code calls `open(url).read` but that file only `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` and does not `require 'open-uri'`. The only added `require 'open-uri'` in this diff is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which is a separate code path. `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` both call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` without requiring `open-uri`, so unless some unrelated part of the app already loaded `open-uri`, `Kernel#open` will treat the URL as a local filename and raise `Errno::ENOENT` (or otherwise fail to fetch HTTP).
